C1.worst_defect: The home page never says who should not use it or how it differs from a hosted till (Shopify POS, Square, Lightspeed): the deal-breakers for a buyer (no card-terminal integration, no cash drawer, iPad and tablets 'not tested yet', one tab per till) sit only in the third bullet of 'Before you start' near the bottom, not near the hero promise 'made for shops that sell online with Vendure and also sell in person'.
C1.where: home/desktop/01 hero vs home/desktop/02 'Before you start'

C2.worst_defect: The site says 'MIT licensed' and 'open-source' in the hero and footer, but self-hosting the till 'needs your own RxDB Premium licence token (RXDB_PREMIUM)'. It never says this is a paid third-party commercial licence or what it costs. It never names who runs app.vendurepos.com, the default till every merchant is sent to, so a client cannot judge the lock-in.
C2.where: home/desktop/02 'Setting up the store' last bullet; connect-a-till/desktop/01; limitations 'Setting up the store'

C3.worst_defect: The fact that the hosted https till can only reach an https store (plain http only for localhost) is not a prerequisite before 'Open https://app.vendurepos.com'. It turns up only after failure, in '9. Troubleshoot' ('Use HTTPS for a remote store'), so a developer pointing it at an http staging server gets stuck at sign-in. The plugin's own 'New POS till key' role also lacks ReadOrder, so order history is refused until you edit the role by hand.
C3.where: quick-start/desktop/03-04 steps 8 and 9; quick-start 'Optional: a device key for each till'

C4.worst_defect: The changelog's 0.2.0 bullet contradicts itself. It says a key with the vendurepos-pos-till role 'does everything a till does' and then, in the same bullet, 'Not in the release notes: in 0.2.0 and 0.3.0 this role has no ReadOrder, so the till's order history is refused'. Six weeks on, the same known gap is still documented as a manual workaround on four pages (quick start, connect a till twice, changelog) rather than fixed.

C5.worst_defect: The 'What it does today' section mixes two boxed cards with buttons ('Keeps selling offline', 'Every sale lands once') with eight unboxed, text-only feature blocks, so the grid looks half finished. The only product image on the home page is the hero, even though At the till has payment, cashier sheet and closure screenshots that would show the register and Z report claims.

C6.worst_defect: At 390 px the home header shows only 'Docs' and 'Live demo'. 'Quick start' and 'At the till' hide behind a bare chevron, and code blocks soft-wrap inside arguments ("generateMigration(config, { name: / 'AddVendurePos', outputDir: / './src/migrations' })"), which reads like real line breaks when copied by eye.

C7.worst_defect: The SoftwareApplication JSON-LD on home has no softwareVersion or dateModified, even though the page itself advertises 'plugin 0.3.0' and the changelog names till app 0.1.0. Everything else (Lighthouse 98/100/100/100, llms.txt, search API, sitemap, real 404 status) is solid.

overall_worst.defect: 'MIT licensed, open-source' is the headline, but leaving the hosted app.vendurepos.com means buying an RxDB Premium licence the site never calls paid or prices, and the site never says who operates the hosted till. A sceptic advising a client sees a till whose only free path depends on an unnamed operator.
overall_worst.where: home/desktop/02 'Setting up the store' last bullet; footer 'MIT licensed'; connect-a-till/desktop/01
overall_worst.fix: On the home page and Limitations, say in one line that RxDB Premium is a paid third-party licence (with a link to its pricing) and name who runs app.vendurepos.com and what happens to a store if it goes away.
